The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the crimes of the Zionist regime against the oppressed people of Palestine, particularly in Gaza, and emphasizes the urgent need for effective action by the international community to stop the genocide and to hold the Zionist criminals accountable and punish them. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also strongly condemns the crimes of the occupying regime and the terrorist acts of Zionist settlers against Palestinians in the West Bank—the most recent of which was the burning of the Al-Dahi Mosque. While Gaza has been turned into a pile of rubble and debris as a result of extensive bombings, and the displaced people of Gaza have been deprived even of access to tents to protect themselves from the cold and rain in the winter cold, Zionist military forces, by storming the center of Gaza, are seeking to intensify the genocide plan and kill more people. The inaction imposed on international institutions by the United States and the supporters of the occupying regime has led to greater insolence by this regime and the continuation of the gross violation of the fundamental rights of the Palestinian people. Without a doubt, the United States and other supporters of the occupying regime—especially Germany as the second-largest arms seller to this regime, as well as the United Kingdom, France, and Canada, which in various ways have shielded this regime from any accountability and punishment—are partners in the crimes committed in Gaza. Furthermore, all parties that were present and participated in the ceasefire agreement of 9 October 2025 in Sharm El-Sheikh bear direct responsibility for stopping the crimes of the occupying regime. The Islamic Republic of Iran recalls the responsibility of all states, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and international law, to support the oppressed people of Palestine in realizing their right to self-determination and liberation from the evil of occupation, apartheid, and brutal colonialism, and emphasizes that all countries, pursuant to the relevant international instruments, particularly the “Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide” and the “Four Geneva Conventions of 1949,” are obligated to take action to stop the genocide and war crimes that are continuously taking place in Gaza and the West Bank. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also condemns the continuous obstruction by the American ruling establishment of the process of addressing the crimes committed by the Zionist regime, especially through the sanctions and intimidation of the judges of the International Criminal Court, and reminds all countries of their responsibility to prosecute and punish the leaders of the Zionist regime for the commission of international crimes. The Islamic Republic of Iran, while emphasizing its all-out support for the Palestinian people until the realization of their right to self-determination and the establishment of an independent Palestinian state with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital, calls on the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and all Islamic countries to take immediate measures to utilize all the capacities of this organization and other international institutions to confront the genocide of the Palestinians.

item.title: Iran slams IAEA chief for double standards on Israeli nuclear arsenal
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baqaei said IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi cannot use Israel’s non-membership in the Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) to evade scrutiny of the agency’s indifference toward the Israeli regime’s nuclear arsenal and its double standards toward Iran’s nuclear program. Baqaei made the remarks in a post on X, criticizing Grossi’s justification of the agency’s different approaches to Iran’s peaceful nuclear program and Israel’s weapons-related nuclear activities.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the aggressive actions carried out by the terrorist US Army against locations along the southern coasts of Iran over the past several days. In response to these acts of aggression, the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran, in exercise of their inherent right to self-defense and in line with their duty to safeguard the country’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity, launched forceful and decisive defensive strikes against Patriot air defense systems and drone and missile launch platforms belonging to the US Army at two of its bases in the region, which had served as the origin and support bases for aggressive operations against the Islamic Republic of Iran. The defensive measures taken by the Islamic Republic of Iran in response to the US armed attacks have been carried out within the framework of its inherent right to self-defense and with the aim of countering the sources and supporting infrastructure of the aggression. It is self-evident that the legal and international responsibility for the consequences of this situation rests with the United States, which, by violating the fundamental principles of international law and resorting unlawfully to the use of force, has endangered regional peace and security. While reaffirming its respect for the national sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly urges the governments of the region to take the necessary measures to prevent aggressors from continuing to use their territories, bases, and facilities located in their countries to plan, prepare, and carry out acts of aggression against Iran. The failure of regional countries to prevent the United States from using their territories and facilities to prepare and carry out acts of aggression against Iran is not only contrary to the principle of good neighborliness, but also constitutes an “act of aggression” under Paragraph (f) of Article 3 of the Annex to United Nations General Assembly Resolution 3314, fully entitling and authorizing Iran to take defensive measures against them. It should be noted that, to date, the Islamic Republic of Iran has acted with the utmost restraint, out of consideration for its relations with neighboring countries and the interests of the Islamic Ummah, and has exclusively targeted US military bases and assets in those countries in its defensive strikes. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran once again underscores the responsibility of the United Nations, particularly the Security Council and the Secretary-General, to fulfill their duties in accordance with the UN Charter. Silence and inaction in the face of the continued violation of the Charter’s fundamental principles, particularly the prohibition on the use of force enshrined in Article 2(4), by a permanent member of the Security Council will not only undermine the credibility and standing of the United Nations, but will also pave the way for further acts of aggression and an escalating threat to international peace and security. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also condemns the irresponsible approach of certain regional parties which, disregarding the realities on the ground and turning a blind eye to the US acts of aggression against Iran, criticize Iran’s legitimate self-defense operations. It calls on these countries to prevent the United States from using their territories and bases in the region to prepare and carry out acts of aggression against Iran, rather than complaining about Iran for exercising its right to self-defense. The Islamic Republic of Iran, reaffirming its firm determination to defend its sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity, declares that any repetition of aggression or hostile action against Iran will be met with a resolute and regret-inducing response from the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran.

item.title: Iran Oman and Uzbekistan hold trilateral foreign ministers’ meeting in Muscat
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is visiting Muscat for an official visit to Oman and consultations with senior Omani officials on bilateral relations and regional developments, attended a trilateral meeting of the foreign ministers of Iran, Oman and Uzbekistan to discuss the potential of the North-South Corridor. The meeting, hosted by Sayyid Badr Al-Busaidi, Foreign Minister of the Sultanate of Oman, was attended by Bakhtiyor Saidov, Foreign Minister of the Republic of Uzbekistan, and Araghchi. The three sides discussed ways to expand interregional cooperation in various economic, trade, transportation and transit sectors. Highlighting the considerable potential of the three countries to expand economic ties, particularly through strengthening trade exchanges along the Central Asia–Persian Gulf/Gulf of Oman route (the North-South Corridor), the foreign ministers of Iran, Uzbekistan and Oman emphasized the importance of planning to expand regional transportation networks and complete and upgrade the relevant infrastructure.

item.title: Iran FM Araghchi receives Qatari delegation in Muscat
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is visiting Muscat for an official visit to Oman, received a Qatari delegation on Tuesday afternoon. The Qatari delegation, headed by an adviser to Qatar’s prime minister, traveled to Oman and held talks with Iran’s foreign minister on the latest regional developments. Referring to Qatar’s continued role in efforts to ease tensions in the region, Araghchi stressed the importance of continued consultations among regional countries to counter the destabilizing and insecurity-inducing activities of actors from outside the region.
